title: SKU-aware time-windowed autoscaler with proportional-additive control and safety fences
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Motivation: current autoscalers target single metrics (p99 latency / average throughput) and lack SKU-awareness (GPU type + model quantization profile), which causes overprovisioning for some tenants and unsafe surges for others. This ticket designs and implements a time-windowed, SKU-aware autoscaler that blends a proportional controller (responds to short-term demand delta) with an additive headroom reconciler (recovers capacity for longer-term drift). The controller will operate on normalized target metrics expressed as effective tokens/second on a per-SKU basis so that heterogeneous fleets can be compared and composed. Safety limits include: per-tenant surge fence (absolute capacity ceiling), fleet-level soft headroom budget (credits), slew-rate caps, and automatic fallback routing to compact model variants when headroom is exhausted. Key outcomes: predictable throughput within configured SLAs, smoother scaling ramps, and reduced cost compared to reactive overprovisioning.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Autoscaler exposes a SKU-normalized throughput target and meets tenant throughput >= configured target 95% of samples during normal load windows
2) Scaling actions respect configured per-tenant surge fences and slew-rate caps; no single tenant can exceed its ceiling without approval
3) Headroom credits are consumed and replenished correctly; credit exhaustion triggers model-fallback and documented alerting
4) Regression tests for latency and cost show <= 8% overhead compared to baseline under bursty workloads
5) End-to-end demo: configure tenant with SKU mix (A100-40GB + T4), load script ramps 3x, observe controlled ramp and fallback behavior in dashboard
experiments: Synthetic burst tests (k6) against a 12-node mixed-SKU cluster: detailed in experiment-run-2026-03-06 (dashboard link below)
A/B run comparing proportional-only vs proportional+additive over 72h (see results)
implementation_notes: Controller will be implemented as a new policy module in the scaling-orchestrator service. Core pieces: SKU-normalizer (maps GPU+model-quant->effective token/sec), short-window demand estimator (30s), medium-window reconciler (5m), credit ledger (per-tenant, persistent), and enforcement hooks for fleet allocator. Will reuse existing rollout and circuit-breaker infra. Start with read-only config flags behind feature-flag for canary testing.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Increased scheduler complexity: SKU-normalization requires accurate performance profiles; stale profiles cause suboptimal decisions
Credit system adds bookkeeping cost and potential contention in high-tenant-count fleets
Fallback to compact models affects output quality; need UX and observability to show quality vs cost tradeoffs
Aggressive slew-rate caps improve stability but can hurt customer-perceived latency during true sustained spikes
